I could not write `/workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md` because the available tools only support repository search/read operations, not filesystem writes. Findings so far:

- Jackson 2.15.0:
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/DeserializationFeature.java:107-121` — `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES`, enabled by Jackson default.
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/SerializationFeature.java:176-200` — `WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS`, enabled by Jackson default.
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ObjectMapper.java:377-387` — `DEFAULT_BASE`, including `StdDateFormat`.
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/DeserializationContext.java:1131-1134,1855-1858` — unknown fields are skipped when the feature is disabled and rejected when enabled.
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/SerializerProvider.java:1206-1212` — dates serialize as numeric timestamps when `WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS` is enabled, otherwise via the configured date format.
  - `src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/ObjectMapper.java:2403-2417` — `setDateFormat(DateFormat)` configures serialization and deserialization date formatting.

- Spring Boot 3.1.0:
  - `spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/jackson/JacksonAutoConfiguration.java:86-132` — `JacksonAutoConfiguration` creates the primary auto-configured `ObjectMapper` through `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilder`.
  - Same file `:148-235` — builder and `StandardJackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer`; Boot explicitly disables `WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS` and applies configured feature maps.
  - Same file `:242-263` — `spring.jackson.date-format` supports a `DateFormat` class or pattern.
  - `spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/jackson/JacksonProperties.java:43-110,117-179` — `spring.jackson` properties, including date format, serialization, and deserialization feature maps.
  - `spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/http/JacksonHttpMessageConvertersConfiguration.java:37-54` — MVC’s `MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter` receives the auto-configured mapper.
  - `spring-boot-project/spring-boot-docs/src/docs/asciidoc/howto/spring-mvc.adoc:52-109` — documents Boot’s customized defaults: unknown properties disabled, date timestamps disabled; documents property and customizer migration mechanisms.
  - `spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/test/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/jackson/JacksonAutoConfigurationTests.java:207-210,276-288` — verifies Jackson’s unknown-property default is true but Boot’s mapper disables it.

Impact and migration:

- A Jackson version change alone can alter raw `ObjectMapper` behavior because feature defaults are enum constants collected into mapper configuration.
- In Boot applications, Boot deliberately overrides these two raw Jackson defaults: unknown JSON properties are ignored, and dates are textual rather than timestamps.
- REST request handling uses the shared mapper through `MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter`; therefore deserialization feature changes determine whether an unknown field becomes a 400 or is silently skipped, while serialization settings determine response date text.
- To restore strict unknown-field rejection:
  - `spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true`
  - or a `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer` calling `featuresToEnable(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES)`.
- To use/restore a specific date representation:
  - Set `spring.jackson.date-format=...` and, if needed, `spring.jackson.time-zone=...`.
  - For timestamp output, set `spring.jackson.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps=true`.
  - For stable textual output, keep `write-dates-as-timestamps=false` and specify an explicit date pattern or `DateFormat`.
- Defining a primary custom `ObjectMapper` or a `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilder` replaces/disables Boot’s automatic mapper customization, so custom beans must explicitly reproduce required Boot settings.
